telegramBot.reason: The sole customer surface displays rates and terms, immediately creates/replaces a durable lock, later reads and atomically consumes it during buy-order creation.

site.reason: No website rate-lock route, template or consumer was observed; current feature contract is Telegram-only.

miniApp.reason: No Mini App rate-lock control, disclosure or status projection was observed.

admin.reason: No Filament model/resource or order projection exposes lock terms, fee, source, replacement or consumption evidence.

api.reason: The internal repository adapter is not a public HTTP contract; no rate-lock API route exists.

native.reason: No native rate-lock UX or contract exists and the feature grants no signing authority.

authorityBoundary.priceAuthority: Bot CoinGecko then Binance cache with static fallback
authorityBoundary.moneyAuthority: Bot-calculated preferred/fallback quote vectors selected by transactional order writer

positiveControls: Active reads bind user, currency, unused state and database-time expiry.
Order creation consumes a lock with an atomic id/user/currency/unused/unexpired compare-and-set in the same transaction.
A lost race or expired lock falls back instead of applying one locked quote twice.
Promo capacity and one-use claim are transactionally selected with explicit no-promo fallback vectors.
Direction availability is checked before creating the lock and again before creating the order.
The proposal-only B4 function rehearses advisory serialization, rollback and execute-only least privilege.

criticalFindings.finding: Telegram twice says 100 RUB will be deducted, but fee_rub is only stored/read. Crypto is calculated from the full RUB amount; the order and accounting contain no lock-fee debit or attribution.

After source failure get_cached_rate can return an arbitrarily old process cache or a static fallback without source, as-of, fallback or confidence metadata; that scalar is persisted as a new 15-minute guarantee.
The ratelock callback has no confirmation, payment, idempotency key, nonce or receipt. Repetition creates a fresh free 15-minute promise and marks prior unused locks used.

Consumption verifies lock ownership/currency/expiry but trusts caller-supplied preferred rate and crypto vectors rather than deriving and validating them from persisted locked_rate, fee, amount and versioned policy.

The deployed PostgreSQL adapter locks only existing rows and the schema has a non-unique partial index, so concurrent first inserts may leave multiple active locks. The advisory-lock function remains proposal-only.

Only the raw market component is frozen. Final rate remains dependent on later amount and promo commission; displayed menu rate and persisted selection are separate reads without quote identity or customer confirmation.
If consumption loses a race or expires, the order silently adopts a regular quote without an explicit renewed customer consent step.

No CHECKs, active uniqueness, order foreign key, provenance, policy version, paid/refunded/replaced reason, audit correlation, retention, deletion or compensation lifecycle exists; used=true conflates replacement and consumption.

independentReviews.finding: Fee is fictional, renewal is free, price provenance fails open, first-insert concurrency is unsafe and DB quote integrity trusts the caller.
Idempotency, provenance, monetary binding, schema constraints, audit/retention and compensation are absent despite positive owner/expiry/CAS controls.
Telegram is the only implemented surface; operator evidence and cross-surface disclosures are absent, and the feature is not a full immutable quote.

nextCanonicalItem: Classify DEPLOYMENT_RELEASE_AUTOMATION across all six surfaces and verify its source trust, credentials, checks, restart authority, audit, rollback and recovery boundary read-only.
